The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

He insisted / for immediate payment / of the two months' / pending electricity bill.
practice.solution: *Insist* pairs with **on**: 'insisted on immediate payment'. Part 3's possessive (*two months'*) is correct as a time-denoting possessive.
practice.shortcut: Insist—on. Recall the pair, not the meaning.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Between you and I, / the newly appointed / manager has no / practical field experience.
practice.solution: A preposition takes object forms: *between you and **me***. *I* is a subject form and cannot follow *between*.
practice.shortcut: Preposition + I is always the error; flip it mentally: 'between me'.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Hardly had / the chief guest arrived / than the power / went off.
practice.solution: *Hardly/Scarcely* pair with **when**; *no sooner* pairs with *than*. The sentence mixes the two pairs: 'Hardly had... **when** the power went off'.
practice.shortcut: Two fixed pairs: hardly...when, no sooner...than. Swapped partners = the answer.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Mumbai is / more bigger / than any other city / in the state.
practice.solution: *Bigger* is already comparative; adding *more* creates a double comparative: *Mumbai is bigger than any other city in the state*. Part 3 is correct — *any other* is exactly what the comparison needs, since Mumbai itself belongs to the group of cities.
practice.shortcut: Double comparative = instant conviction: -er and 'more' cannot coexist.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The exhausted traveller / returned back / to the hotel / a little after midnight.
practice.solution: *Return* already contains the idea of coming back; *back* is redundant: *returned to the hotel*. Redundant pairs are planted answers — return back, repeat again, revert back.
practice.shortcut: Hear the pair: return + back repeats one idea. Strike the second word.

practice.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The interviewer asked / my friend that why / he had left / his previous job.
practice.solution: After *asked*, the reported clause drops **that** when the question word *why* introduces it: 'asked my friend why he had left'. *That* and *why* cannot introduce the same clause. (The backshift to *had left* in part 3 is correct.)
practice.shortcut: In indirect questions, the wh-word alone introduces the clause — 'asked that why' doubles the introducer.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The true subject is **the number** (singular); *applicants* sits inside the 'of' phrase and cannot decide the verb. Part 2 must read **has doubled**. The other parts are grammatical.
practice.shortcut: Cover the 'of' phrase; the number is singular.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: 'Along with' only adds information; the subject stays **the manager** (singular), so part 2 needs **was inspecting**. Parts 3 and 4 are correct.
practice.shortcut: as well as / along with → verb follows the first subject.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: After the helper **did**, the base form is required: part 2 must be **end** ('did the lecture end'). The no-sooner…than frame in parts 3 and 4 is correctly built.
practice.shortcut: did + base verb; than pairs with no sooner.

practice.q: Three parts of a sentence are given in order, followed by a fourth option. If there is no error anywhere, select 'No error'.
practice.solution: **Has been living** is a correct present perfect continuous; **since her marriage** correctly gives a point of time with *since*. No part breaks a rule → **No error**.
practice.shortcut: since + point of time is correct; run the checks before choosing No error.

practice.q: Three parts of a sentence are given in order, followed by a fourth option. If there is no error anywhere, select 'No error'.
practice.solution: **Each** is unconditionally singular; the plural *students* inside the 'of' phrase cannot change that. Part 2 must read **was given**.
practice.shortcut: each of + plural noun → singular verb.

practice.q: Three parts of a sentence are given in order, followed by a fourth option. If there is no error anywhere, select 'No error'.
practice.solution: **Hardly** means 'almost not' — the intended meaning needs the adverb of effort **hard**: 'working hard since morning'. The perfect form in parts 1 and 3 is correct.
practice.shortcut: hardly = almost never; hard = with effort.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Part 1 looks wrong because *products* sits next to the verb, but the subject is **the quality** — part 1 is innocent. Part 2 breaks the rule: it must read **has improved**. Name the rule before you pick.
practice.shortcut: Two suspects: the 'of' phrase is a decoy; have → has is the real error.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Part 1 feels odd ('had' with no participle?) but the no-sooner frame is right so far. Part 2 breaks the rule: after *had* the participle must follow — **the results had been declared**. Convict by rule, not by feel.
practice.shortcut: No sooner had + subject + been + participle.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Part 3 looks like a clash, but 'only yesterday' sits perfectly with the simple past **returned** in part 1 — except that part 1 doubles the idea: **return** already means come back, so 'returned back' is redundant. Part 1 is the error.
practice.shortcut: 'Yesterday' is legal with simple past; return back doubles the idea.

practice.q: Each option is a fragment of a different sentence. Exactly one fragment contains an error. Select it.
options: The news of the floods have reached
The furniture in these rooms is
Neither of the two answers is
practice.solution: **News** is singular even though it ends in -s → the news **has** reached. Furniture, mathematics and 'neither of' are all singular subjects with singular verbs — the other three fragments are correct.
practice.shortcut: news, mathematics, furniture → singular.

practice.q: Each option is a fragment of a different sentence. Exactly one fragment contains an error. Select it.
options: The commander-in-chief, with his soldiers, was
Each of the participants have received
The poet and philosopher has written
Ten kilometres is a long walk
practice.solution: **Each** of the participants → singular → each **has** received. 'With his soldiers' leaves the first noun as subject, 'the poet and philosopher' names one person (has), and a distance as one unit takes *is* — all correct.
practice.shortcut: each of → singular; with-phrase is a decoy.

practice.q: Each option is a fragment of a different sentence. Exactly one fragment contains an error. Select it.
options: One of my cousins have settled
The jury was divided in its opinion
Bread and butter is his usual breakfast
Either of the two options is acceptable
practice.solution: The subject is **one** → one **has** settled. 'The jury was…its' (one body), 'bread and butter' (one dish, singular) and 'either of…is' (either of → singular) are all correct fragments.
practice.shortcut: one of + plural noun → singular verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The subject is **one**; 'of the laptops displayed at the expo' only describes it. One → singular → one **was sold**. Part 3 is the error.
practice.shortcut: one of + plural noun + singular verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Every one** points to the sweets one at a time → singular: every one **was wrapped**. The plural *sweets* in part 1 is a decoy.
practice.shortcut: every one of → singular.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: With either…or, the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject — *his cousins* (plural) → **are going to carry**. Part 2 wrongly agrees with Ramesh.
practice.shortcut: either…or → verb follows the nearer subject.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Neither…nor → the nearer subject decides: *his assistants* is plural → **were available**. Part 3 followed the distant 'collector' instead.
practice.shortcut: neither…nor → nearer subject: assistants were.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Many a + singular noun** is grammatically singular even though the meaning is plural → many a student **has failed**. Part 2 is the error.
practice.shortcut: many a → singular verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: When *every* repeats before both nouns, the subject stays singular: every man and every woman **was counted**. The pair feeling in part 1 tempts the plural, but the rule holds.
practice.shortcut: every…and every… → singular.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **A number of** means 'many' → plural: a number of students **were absent**. ('The number of' would take *was* — the article is the whole story.)
practice.shortcut: a number of → plural; the number of → singular.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: after the new signals were installed.
practice.solution: **The number of** names a single count → singular: the number **has fallen**. Part 3 agreed with *accidents* and missed the article.
practice.shortcut: the number of → singular verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: An *until*-clause about the future takes the **simple present**: 'until the cultural programme **concludes**'. *Will* belongs only in the main clause (part 2).
practice.shortcut: until/when/if + future meaning → present tense.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: After **as soon as** with future meaning, use the simple present: 'as soon as I **reach** home'. The main clause keeps *will return*.
practice.shortcut: as soon as + present, never will.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Fifteen years** is a length of time → **for fifteen years**. *Since* needs a point (*since 2011*, *since childhood*). 'Since fifteen years' is the planted error.
practice.shortcut: for + length; since + point.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The knowing began in the past, so the *since*-clause must be past too: 'since we **were** children'. Part 1's present perfect correctly stretches to now.
practice.shortcut: since-clause of a present perfect → past tense.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: so we watched from the back.
practice.solution: The play started **before** we reached — the earlier of two past events takes the past perfect: the play **had already begun**. Part 1's simple past marks the later event correctly.
practice.shortcut: earlier past event → had + participle.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: 'By the time' with a past main clause needs a past verb: **we reached** the venue. *Will* drags a future clause into a past story.
practice.shortcut: by the time + past after a past main clause.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: and have helped her in the kitchen.
practice.solution: Both actions sit inside the closed slot 'last Sunday', so the second verb also takes the simple past: and **helped** her in the kitchen. The perfect form in part 4 clashes with the finished-time anchor.
practice.shortcut: and joins two actions in the same closed time slot → both simple past.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Two days ago** is a finished time → simple past: Ravi **left** for Hyderabad two days ago. The present perfect refuses 'ago'.
practice.shortcut: ago → simple past, never has left.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: A universal truth keeps the **simple present** even after a past reporting verb: the earth **moves** around the sun. Sequence of tenses has this standing exception.
practice.shortcut: general truth → present, even in reported past.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: A scientific fact takes the simple present: water **boils** at 100 degrees Celsius. The continuous form wrongly ties the fact to this moment.
practice.shortcut: general truth → simple present, not continuous.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **University** begins with a consonant sound (yoo-) → **a university**. The letter 'u' is a decoy; the sound decides.
practice.shortcut: u with a y-sound takes a, not an.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **MLA** is read em-el-ay — a vowel sound first → **an MLA's convoy**. Note that 'an hour' in part 2 is correct (silent h).
practice.shortcut: abbreviations follow their first sound: an MLA, a BA.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: A superlative always takes **the**: **the holiest** of the rivers. 'A holiest' is impossible — indefinites cannot single out a top item.
practice.shortcut: superlative → the.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Best** is a superlative → **the best exercise**. The rest of the sentence is correct.
practice.shortcut: a best / a most → always the.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The fixed pair is **capable of** + -ing: 'capable **of handling** this difficult client'. 'Capable to handle' breaks the frozen pair.
practice.shortcut: capable of + -ing; afraid of, fond of.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The fixed pair is **accused of**: accused **of accepting** bribes. 'Accused for' mixes it with 'punished for'.
practice.shortcut: accuse OF, but punish FOR.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The fixed pair is **comply with**: he complied **with the rules**. ('Abide by' takes by, but comply does not — the decoy borrows it.)
practice.shortcut: comply WITH; abide BY.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The idiom is **jump to conclusions**: 'jump **to** conclusions about my honesty'. 'Into' is the planted preposition.
practice.shortcut: jump to conclusions — fixed idiom.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: After the preposition **between**, the object form is required: between Ravi and **him**. 'Between you and I' style errors are the most planted in this slot.
practice.shortcut: preposition → object pronoun: me/him/them.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: After **let**, the object form follows: Let you and **me** resolve this. ('You and I' sounds polite, which is exactly the trap.)
practice.shortcut: let + object form.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: In the clause 'we met ___', the lawyer receives the action (we met **him**) → the object relative **whom**: 'The lawyer **whom** we met yesterday'.
practice.shortcut: him-test: we met him → whom.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Possession needs **whose**, even for things: 'The building **whose** roof was damaged'. 'Which roof' would mean 'choose a roof' — a different sentence entirely.
practice.shortcut: whose = of which; which roof ≠ whose roof.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: With not only…but also, the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject — *his officers* (plural) → **were present**. Part 3 agreed with the distant 'minister'.
practice.shortcut: not only…but also → nearer subject decides the verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: No sooner had the train left
practice.solution: The frozen pair is **no sooner…than**: 'No sooner had the train left **than** the passengers began…'. 'When' belongs with hardly/scarcely.
practice.shortcut: no sooner…THAN; hardly…WHEN.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: For **two** people the reciprocal is **each other**: 'borrowed **each other's** notes'. 'One another' is reserved for more than two.
practice.shortcut: two → each other; many → one another.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **It's** = it is; the possessive is **its**: 'its annual report'. Expand the apostrophe version aloud — 'it is annual report' collapses at once.
practice.shortcut: its = possessive; it's = it is.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: A reported wh-question keeps the wh-word and drops 'that': 'asked the witness **why** he had changed'. 'That why' welds two connectives together.
practice.shortcut: asked + why (no that); asked + whether (no that).

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: A reported yes/no question takes **whether** (or if) alone: 'wanted to know **whether** I had locked'. 'That whether' stacks two connectives.
practice.shortcut: whether / if alone — never 'that whether'.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: One shape only: **better** (already comparative) — 'more better' doubles the marker. The correct part reads simply '**is better** than the last one's'.
practice.shortcut: better = comparative; never more better.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Two** items → comparative: **the shorter** of the two routes. 'Most shortest' doubles the superlative and wrong-counts the comparison. (Part 4's 'the safer' is correct for two items.)
practice.shortcut: two → the …er of; three+ → the …est of.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Repeat** already means 'say again' → 'repeat again' doubles the idea. The clean form: 'Please repeat what you said'.
practice.shortcut: repeat, return, revert — never add again/back.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Both** already means 'the two of you' → 'both of you two' counts twice. The clean form: '**Both of you** agree' (or 'you both agree').
practice.shortcut: both + two = one idea twice.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The slot needs the **verb** 'to influence' → **affect**: 'will adversely **affect** your appetite'. *Effect* is the noun (a result).
practice.shortcut: affect = verb; effect = noun.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Needed meaning: misplace → **lose**. *Loose* means 'not tight' and *loosen* means 'make less tight' — neither fits.
practice.shortcut: lose (misplace) / loose (not tight).

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The slot is a noun (the subject of 'changed') → **advice**: 'the principal's firm **advice**'. *Advise* is the verb (to advise).
practice.shortcut: advice = noun; advise = verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Nagpur is itself a city of Maharashtra, so it must not be compared with itself: harsher than **any other city** in Maharashtra.
practice.shortcut: member vs own group → any other.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Latin comparatives take **to**, never than: superior **to**, senior to, junior to, prior to, preferable to. Part 1 must read 'superior **to**'.
practice.shortcut: superior/senior/junior/prior/preferable → to.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: In **look forward to**, the word 'to' is a preposition, so it takes the -ing form: 'looking forward **to seeing** the circus'. 'Look forward to see' is the classic slip.
practice.shortcut: look forward to + -ing (to is a preposition here).

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Deny** takes the -ing form: 'She denied **having taken** the file'. Verbs like deny, enjoy, avoid and suggest refuse the infinitive.
practice.shortcut: deny / enjoy / avoid / suggest + -ing.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The statement uses **have** with the subject *the students* → the tag flips it: **haven't they?** 'Isn't it?' matches neither the helper nor the subject.
practice.shortcut: tag = helping verb flipped + subject pronoun.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Rarely** makes the statement negative, so the tag must be positive: **does he?** 'Doesn't he' fails to flip — the same trap hides behind never, seldom, hardly and little.
practice.shortcut: rarely / never / hardly → positive tag.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The unreal-past conditional takes **had** + participle in the if-clause: '**If I had known** about the traffic'. 'Would have' stays in the main clause only.
practice.shortcut: if + had known; main clause keeps would have.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: The if-clause of a real future condition takes the **simple present**: 'If she **works** hard'. *Will* appears only in the main clause.
practice.shortcut: if + present; will in the main clause.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: and to speed up file movement.
practice.solution: The list runs on -ing forms after 'aims at': reducing, improving, and **speeding up**. 'To speed up' breaks the parallel line.
practice.shortcut: lists stay parallel: match the first item's shape.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
options: and long walks in the park.
practice.solution: After **enjoys**, every item takes the -ing shape: cooking, **gardening**, and (taking) long walks. 'To garden' is the odd form out.
practice.shortcut: enjoy + -ing for every item in the list.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Runs** is an action verb, so it is described by an adverb: runs very **smoothly**. (Part 3's 'hardly' is correct — a hidden negative fits here.)
practice.shortcut: action verb → adverb: runs smoothly.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Taste** here is a linking verb describing the mangoes, so it takes the adjective: they taste **delicious**. 'Taste deliciously' would describe how the mangoes perform the action of tasting.
practice.shortcut: linking verbs (taste, smell, feel) → adjective.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: **Could** already carries ability, so only the bare verb follows: 'could not **explain** the gap'. 'Could able to' doubles the idea and breaks the grammar.
practice.shortcut: never 'could able to' — could + base verb.

practice.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
practice.solution: Modals take the bare base verb: 'You must **submit** the completed form'. No 'to' after must, can, should or could.
practice.shortcut: modal + base verb, no to.
